EXECUTIVE ORDER 9514
Amending  E xecutive  O rder 9452 A uthor ­
izing  the  S ecretary  of S tate to P re­
scribe  R egulations  and I ssue  O rders 
and I nstructions  R elating  to the  
F oreign  S ervice of the  U nited  S tates
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by sections 202 and 
1752 of the Revised Statutes of the 
United States (5 U.S.C. 156; 22 U.S.C. 
132), and as President of the United 
States, it is hereby ordered that section 
1  of Executive Order 9452 of June 26, 
1944 (9 PR. 7183) be amended to read 
as follows:
1. The Secretary of State is,author­
ized to prescribe such regulations and 
issue such orders and instructions, not 
inconsistent with the Constitution, any 
law of the United States, or any Execu­
tive order or proclamation, relating to 
the duties of officers and employees of 
the Foreign Service of the United States 
and the transaction of their business, as 
he may deem conducive to the public 
interest: Provided, however, that the au­
thority granted by this order shall not 
be exercised in any case in which the 
President' is specifically authorized by 
any law other than section, 1752 of the 
Revised Statutes (22 U.S.C. 132), to pre­
scribe regulations with respect to a par­
ticular subject. ♦
F ranklin  D R oosevelt
T he  W hite  H ouse , /
January 18, 1945.

before: EO 9452 creates an indefinite Foreign Service regulatory delegation and a publication delegation, subject to the original broad prohibition where the President has specific statutory rulemaking authority and to independent publication law. The complete high-confidence official extract contains no own-term expiry, report-triggered cessation or unaccounted operative provision. Paragraph 1 is split into its grant and proviso because EO 9514, signed January 18, 1945 without delayed effectiveness, reenacts the grant but narrows the proviso to permit exercise of Revised Statutes section 1752 authority. The original unqualified proviso therefore first ends in its original form on January 18, 1945; the grant, remaining limitation in its amended form, and paragraph 2 continue. EO 9521 is not a revoker of this target: its preamble acknowledges EO 9452 as amended and its revocation list names other orders. The actual 1945 State regulation discovered in a neighboring-document extract is a use of the amended delegation, not evidence of cessation or revival. EO 12292 section 10(a) revokes EO 9452, and section 11 expressly makes that action effective as of February 15, 1981, rather than its February 23 signature or February 25 publication. This is the last end among the original operative units. The sole current USC mention reproduces that revocation and supplies no continuing predicate. Strong complete official extracts plus matching official GPO fixity establish the read text; no PDF page image verification is asserted. The provisional whole-order status remains no.
